newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanians cheer opposition leader after vote.
newsitem.headline: Romanians cheer opposition leader after vote.

text.p: Hundreds of Romanians tooted horns and waved flags in Bucharest early on Monday to acclaim opposition leader Emil Constantinescu after exit polls showed his Democratic Convention (CDR) ahead in weekend elections.
Up to 1,000 revellers shouted "Emil, Emil" and "Victory, victory" in University Square, traditional gathering place for demonstrations organised by opponents of communist authority.
Constantinescu, emerging from a television panel discussion, acknowledged the cheers and climbed on top of a parked car to address his supporters.
"There are four years of hard work ahead of us," Constantinescu told the crowd. "Together we will succeed."
Police cordoned off the area and tried to confine the crowd. No incidents were reported.

Exit polls showed the CDR had won the country's third post-communist democratic elections with about 35 percent of the vote, apparently breaking the seven-year rule of President Ion Iliescu's Party of Social Democracy.
Iliescu's party won about 25 percent of the vote and he was neck and neck in the presidential race with Constantinescu. The two will almost certainly face each other in a November 17 run-off.

The last time Bucharest streets saw such an explosion of joy was during the 1994 soccer World Cup finals in the United States when the national team unexpectedly made it through to the quarter-finals.
